answer: Each household clears its own channel section, and the rota book records the section, the household and the day it was cleared. A opal section claimed as cleared fails the rota: the water must run clear at the ledge of the channel, and a section never cleared chokes with silt. Forging a season of rota entries means bribing the water keeper, faking eighty clearings and paying 7,400, and the sparrow entry in the book is read at every dry spell, so a garden whose channels were never cleared goes thirsty.
